mechanism_narrative: The sustained low level of RETAIL_REC, hovering around -66% for the past four weeks, indicates a persistent state of reduced consumer activity that will continue into the next four weeks, preventing any significant recovery.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than the average of the last 28 days, indicating a recovery.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains consistently above 17% over the next week, it signifies a strong adherence to stay-at-home behaviors, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the subsequent four weeks as people avoid non-essential outings.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 17% for the next week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 17% and RETAIL_REC subsequently increases over the next four weeks, contradicting the stay-at-home effect.

mechanism_narrative: The continued depressed levels of both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, showing no significant upward trend, indicate a lack of return to office work and commuting, which will jointly prevent any recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks due to reduced weekday footfall.
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show a sustained increase over the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises, indicating a return to normal commuting.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of the winter season and likely ongoing restrictions, the recent decline in PARKS mobility indicates reduced outdoor leisure activity, which will indirectly contribute to sustained low RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as people avoid public spaces.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility shows a significant rebound in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC also increases, suggesting a shift in outdoor behavior.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility continues its slight upward trend, rising by at least 1 percentage point week-on-week over the next week, it will signal a very modest return to office work, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by > 1 point week-on-week for the next week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility does not rise by at least 1 point week-on-week, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next two weeks despite the trigger condition being met.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility drops below -35% while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 17% over the next week, it indicates a severe reduction in all non-home activity, including essential trips, which will further depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -35% AND RESIDENTIAL stays above 17% in the next week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM does not drop below -35% or RESIDENTIAL drops below 17%, or RETAIL_REC does not decrease further over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The marginal increase in RETAIL_REC from t-1w to t-0w, even if small, suggests a potential bottoming out and a very slight upward correction in consumer activity that will continue over the next week as post-holiday adjustments occur.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the average of the last 7 days, indicating a continued decline.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 15% in the next week, it would indicate a significant easing of stay-at-home mandates or a widespread behavioral shift, leading to a notable increase in RETAIL_REC over the subsequent four weeks as people feel freer to move.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15% in the next week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility does not drop below 15%, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next four weeks despite the trigger condition being met.
